C0.quote: when it is possible for the organizers to fix a bracket

C1.quote: complexity of deciding whether a manipulation is possible
C1.note: Primary is tournament fixing/manipulation; algorithmic complexity also main results.

C2.1.quote: We are given a tournament graph T = (V, E)

C2.2.quote: indicates the winner of any pairwise matchup
C2.2.note: Input is pairwise match outcomes; bracket is organizer-chosen.

C2.3.note: No voters or held attitudes are modelled; players are alternatives with fixed pairwise outcomes.

C2.4.quote: We are given a tournament graph T = (V, E)
C2.4.note: No held attitude is referred to; the input is the given tournament graph.

C3.1.note: No voters are modelled, so no voter strategic misreporting is analysed.

C4.1.note: C2.2 includes PAIR but no utility/welfare/satisfaction/cost/distortion notions for voters are used.

C4.2.note: Term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.note: No welfare, efficiency, satisfaction, representation, proportionality, or distortion criterion is used.

CAN.note: Not present: players are alternatives, not acting candidates.

ORG.quote_behav: the organizers to fix a bracket to help their preferred player win
ORG.quote_info: given the knowledge of which player would win in any pairwise matchup
ORG.note: Organizer chooses bracket to make preferred player win.

BRI.note: Not present; organizer is not an external briber.

C8.1.quote: there exists a valid bracket that makes our desired winner x win
C8.1.note: Tournament fixing is a manipulation/control decision problem.
